abstract: We provide a method to construct a real-analytic ideal MHD equilibrium $(B,p)$ in a solid toroidal domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{3}$, with $B$ tangential to the boundary $\partial\Omega$. The regular pressure level sets foliate $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ by nested tori surrounding a magnetic axis $\Gamma$, with $\nabla p\neq0$ away from the axis. We construct an example where the magnetic field is nonvanishing on $\Omega$, and the rotational transform equals 2 on every regular pressure surface. The equilibrium has a trivial Euclidean symmetry group. It is non-isolated in the sense that it belongs to a real-analytic one-parameter family connecting it to an axisymmetric equilibrium. The toroidal domain, magnetic field and pressure vary smoothly along this family. Under the MHD--Euler correspondence, the construction also yields a real-analytic steady incompressible Euler flow with a nonconstant Bernoulli function. This constructively disproves one formulation of Grad's conjecture by exhibiting a smooth toroidal MHD equilibrium with nested pressure surfaces whose Euclidean symmetry group is trivial.
hook: A plasma equilibrium with no symmetry at all is built, disproving one form of Grad's conjecture.
hook_turn: disproving one form of Grad's conjecture.
summary: The authors construct a real-analytic ideal MHD equilibrium in a solid torus with nested pressure surfaces and a trivial symmetry group, and it connects smoothly to an axisymmetric one. Through the MHD-Euler correspondence it also gives a steady Euler flow. This is a mathematical existence result for one formulation of the conjecture, not a design for a fusion device.
title: An Analytic Toroidal MHD Equilibrium with Trivial Euclidean Symmetry Group
